why: No author repository or code link is provided, so there is no released implementation to run or repair. The experiment is nonetheless a small classical NLP pipeline (TF-IDF plus LinearSVC) that can be reimplemented directly from the paper and claim contract on this CPU-only machine.
missing_artifacts: Author code/implementation: no repository, archive, or code link is provided.
CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian Train/Development/Test split files: described in the paper but no direct URL or checksum is given.
Exact label mapping and tropical-cyclone subset construction details needed to match C6/C7 exactly.
blockers_seen: No author code was released or linked.
The dataset acquisition path is underspecified in the paper; CrisisBench v1.0 must be located manually.
No GPU is available, but this is not a blocker for sparse TF-IDF and LinearSVC.

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 10-20 minutes of command time, dominated by obtaining/preparing CrisisBench and fitting a few sparse TF-IDF plus LinearSVC models; the reported vectorization and fitting times are only a few seconds per model.

compute.basis: The target is one sparse word TF-IDF fit on about 70k short texts plus a LinearSVC fit, with reported sub-5-second vectorization/training times; runtime is dominated by dataset download and preparation, not model computation.
